additional_info.subject: ID0475923-DC/Si-D/NO-[MP / PN 170001094] KF214 faulty CRM:03209000146
additional_info.body:
Dear Service Coordinator / RC,
I am writing to inform that we are moving the case
0475923
﻿from the Technical Support to the eMobility RC-NO SI E Queue. We kindly ask you to take over the case and perform the necessary troubleshooting steps.
Customer:
Product:
Sicharge D - Charging Center
Main Asset:
MP / PN 170001094
Charger ID / Serial No.:
Charger address/functional location: Norway
Priority:
Medium
Handover reason: KF212 and KF211
After checking the error flags, we can see that the problem is related to
KF212 KF 211
. In this case, we have two options:
Remote option:
Restart the charger so the code can make the charger work normally. However, there is a risk that this might make the charger stop working completely.
On-site option:
Go to the charger and check if the
KF212 KF 211 internet cable
is connected correctly. If it’s not, replace the cable from
KF212 to KF211
. If the problem still persists, replace
KF212 KF 211
itself.
Kindly pick up the case using "Pick" option in the queue or manually using the "Assign" function from the
eMobility RC-NO SI E Queue
and work on it & document the activity (Logs/Field Service Report) and attach it to the case under Documents Tab on ISP.
In case you require Expert Support, kindly create Work-order as per
unified service process
. If you need assistance with ordering Expert Support, feel free to reach out to Sousa, Afonso (SI E CS SD) at
afonso-sousa@siemens.com
or Teodoso, Rui (SI E CS SD ES) at
rui.teodoso@siemens.com
.
Kindly close the case post resolution following the case handling guidelines.
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Technical Support Team –
Priscilla van Wettum
Please do not change the subject line when replying to this email.

additional_info.subject: RC-Note 06.02
additional_info.body: Troubleshooting from field: TB210 seems to be broken with full load connected. With full load FC212,213 and 214 all units blinking on LED and measured on DC out on TB210 and voltage jumping from 0-24V all the time. We removed the load and with only F212 connected, turned on TB210 again and we get stable voltage. If we connect more than FC212 TB210 start to jump with voltage again, indicating a problem with connected load. We see some glue? and miscolor on TB210 indicating heat inside TB210
